chunks: I (have come to) confirm the truth of the Torah which was sent down before me, and make certain things lawful which have been forbidden until now; and I come to you with a sign from your Lord; so be fearful of God and follow me.

key_terms.التَّوْرَاةِ: The Torah, the scripture revealed to Prophet Moses (AS)
key_terms.لِأُحِلَّ: To make lawful/permissible (abrogation of previous prohibitions)

ai.seo_question: What are the three main purposes of the Prophet's mission mentioned in this verse regarding the Torah and divine signs?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for establishing the continuity of prophethood, where Muhammad (PBUH) confirms the Torah while introducing new legal dispensations (naskh) and presenting the 'sign' (ayah) as his own person or the Quran. It underscores the divine command to obey the Prophet as an extension of fearing God, reinforcing the concept of his authoritative leadership (Imamah) within the broader framework of Islamic jurisprudence.
